Bhojadeva
or Bhojarāja or Bhoja, son of Sindhula; king of Dhārā, capital of Vidarbha; also called Dhāreśavara an. Vidarbharāja. For details, see Kane, HDS. I. ii. Sn. 65.
mentioned by Daśabala, Oxf. 328a; by Śulapāṇi in Prāyaścittaviveka, Oxf. 283a; by Allāḍanātha in Nirṇayāmṛta, Weber 1170; q. by Sāyaṇa in Alaṅkārasudhānidhi, see ABORI. Golden Jubilee Vol.. XLVIII. an. XLIX. p. 276.
mentioned a. a medical writer in Bhāvaprakāśa, Oxf. 311b; by Mādhava in Rugviniścaya. Oxf. 314b;
mentioned a. a. astronomer by Keśavārka in Vivāhavṛndāvana, Oxf. 336b; a. a grammanan an. lexicographer, he is noticed by Kṣīrasvāmin an. Mahīpa in Nānārtharatnatilaka, Oxf. 352a; is praised by the poets Chittapa, Deveśvara, Vināyaka, Śaṅkara, Sarasvatīkuḍumbaduhitṛ.
His verses are q. in various anthologies. in Śp. v.. 809. 842. 993. 1004. 1147. 3827. 3884. 3933; in Vidyākarasahasraka, v.. 18. 780.
The works mentioned here are prob. attributed to him, an. not written by him. It is also believed that most of the works [Page270b] mentioned here are written by Cittapa, his court poet.
